messages:
sophie: FYI — ArgoScope (new sales opp) just asked for a 6mo Dedicated commit in eu-west. Baseline traffic ~200 A100-equivalent GPU-hours/day but they expect marketing-driven spikes up to ~3x for 2–3 week windows per quarter. Can infra recommend a sizing + buffer policy?
leo: They want an SLA for latency and want burst to be guaranteed during campaign windows. Sales asked for options: fixed commit + burst credits, or a sliding reserve multiplier.
marcus: Quick Q: is the 200 GPU-hours/day their steady-state or the daily average across users? Need conversion to GPUs for capacity planning (hours -> GPUs * 24h).
jiayi: They gave hourly distribution: steady-state ~8.3 GPU-hours/hr (~200/day), peaks up to ~25 GPU-hours/hr during campaigns (3x). For planning I translate to GPUs as: steady-state ~= 0.35 GPUs continuous, peak ~= 1.05 GPUs continuous. But we sell in whole GPU units and want headroom.
rene: Also note eu-west datacenter has an AZ IP/ENI limit we've hit before for similar reserved pools — if we reserve many instances we may need to stagger AZ placement or request quota bump. That affects how much we can promise as 'guaranteed' burst.
arun: From pricing/finance: customer prefers predictable monthly charge. We should show cost delta between committing more baseline vs offering burst credits. Breakdown helps negotiation.
marcus: Proposal idea: tiered commit model — commit to N GPUs baseline (monthly), plus a small guaranteed burst pool (M GPUs) for campaign windows, then an overflow best-effort tier that falls back to hosted. Example numbers below.
marcus: ```
# rough calc for a 30-day month
baseline_gpu_hours = 200/day * 30 = 6000 GPU-hours/month
if we size baseline as 3 x A100 (3 GPUs running 24/7): 3*24*30 = 2160 GPU-hours -> insufficient
so we should size in terms of concurrency not just hours. For 200 GPU-hours/day that indicates ~0.35 avg GPUs continuous -> rounding up to 1 GPU baseline makes sense for latency SLAs
Campaign spikes (3x) -> ~1.05 GPUs continuous -> round up to 2 GPUs guaranteed burst for 3-week windows
Monthly commit options: baseline=1 GPU + guaranteed-burst=2 GPUs for campaign windows + overflow burst credits
```
jiayi: That code-block math is a little confusing because GPU-hours/day to continuous GPUs is: continuous_gpus = GPU-hours/day / 24. So 200/24 ~ 8.33, wait that's wrong — double-check units. I think their "GPU-hours" were already aggregated differently. Sophie — can you paste the raw usage export?
sophie: pasted raw CSV to the thread (sales notes): daily_consumption kol: [200, 220, 250, spikes 600] — those numbers are tokenized estimate from their model. Sorry about the mix. To be explicit: they expect sustained 200 GPU-hours/day (aggregate across jobs), with short windows hitting 600 GPU-hours/day.
marcus: OK with that: 200 GPU-hours/day => 8.33 GPU-hours/hr average -> continuous_gpus = 200/24 = 8.33 GPUs continuous. That makes more sense — earlier I was reading per-hour numbers incorrectly. So baseline is ~8–9 GPUs continuous. Peak ~600/24 = 25 GPUs continuous. That scales differently.
leo: Right — they're heavy. So commit numbers should be in the 10s of GPUs. Sales asked what's a reasonable buffer % vs an absolute burst pool.
rene: Given eu-west AZ constraints and typical failure domains, we should avoid putting whole burst pool in a single AZ. Recommend guaranteed burst distributed across 3 AZs (rounding up). Also network egress limits can throttle in heavy campaigns; add note for customer that cross-AZ spikes may experience <5% traffic shaping unless quota bump is requested.
arun: Cost math: committing extra baseline GPUs reduces per-unit price. Two options to present: (A) Commit to 12 GPUs baseline (covers moderate spikes) with 30% burst credit bucket; (B) Commit to 9 GPUs baseline + guaranteed 16 GPU burst for 3 weeks per quarter, overflow best-effort. We should show monthly price delta.
marcus: Operational considerations: autoscaling within Dedicated pool is allowed but autoscale time to spin GPUs is ~2–4m for warm nodes, cold starts longer. For campaign windows they want immediate availability — so guaranteed burst must be pre-provisioned (hot). Otherwise they risk latency regressions.
jiayi: Suggested engineering policy for this customer: 1) baseline commit = 10 GPUs, 2) guaranteed hot burst = 20 GPUs reserved during campaign windows (scheduled canary start), 3) overflow up to +30 GPUs best-effort that falls back to hosted and is metered. This gives headroom and price tiers.
sophie: Sales note: ArgoScope will likely push back on a large upfront commit. They prefer a seasonal ramp plan with option to autoscale commitments each quarter. We should offer a ramp: months 1–2: 6 GPUs baseline, months 3–4: 10 GPUs, months 5–6: 15 GPUs, with fixed burst credits. Thoughts?
marcus: Ramp is fine but we must include a minimum guaranteed hot burst during campaign windows — otherwise we can't meet SLA. Suggest contractual clause: if campaign expected >X GPUs/day we require a 14-day notice to pre-warm an additional Y GPUs or we bill burst pre-warm fee.
rene: I'll flag the ENI/quota risk and pre-request a capacity reservation with cloud provider if customer signs. If we pre-reserve, we need to pass some of that cost to customer or amortize across months.
arun: I'll model three pricing scenarios and share numbers tomorrow: conservative (low commit + high burst price), balanced (mid commit + moderate burst), aggressive (high commit discount). Sophie — can you confirm campaign cadence and exact weeks per quarter?
sophie: Confirmed: each quarter they run up to 3-week marketing campaigns that usually occur once per quarter, not overlapping. I'll send calendar windows.
marcus: Action items: @rene start cloud quota check for eu-west for up to 60 GPUs across reserved pools. @arun run pricing scenarios and show monthly P&L. @jiayi produce headroom policy text we can put in SOW: pre-warm lead times, burst vs overflow semantics, and AZ distribution requirements. @sophie collect exact campaign dates and expected daily GPU-hours for each.
oncall-bot: Scheduled maintenance notice — eu-west GPU pool will have a rolling kernel upgrade next month; consider bumping pre-warm windows outside maintenance days.
sophie: Thanks all — I'll loop in legal for SOW language once jiayi drafts. We'll aim to deliver an options deck to ArgoScope by EOW. :thumbsup:
